jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR JOB DESCRIPTION

Location:
Los Angeles, CA
Job Type:
Full-Time, hybrid

About LocoL
Alta Community (dba LocoL) is a nonprofit in Watts, which provides culinary job training and education for young people while addressing food insecurity through the preparation and distribution of affordable, high-quality meals, primarily for local nonprofits. Founded as a nonprofit in 2023 by chefs Keith Corbin and Daniel Patterson, LocoL is on the site of the former LocoL restaurant, originally founded by chefs Roy Choi and Daniel Patterson. 

Position Summary

The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and has overall authority and accountability for organizational strategy, personnel, operations, programs, fundraising, and financial management, within policies and budgets approved by the Board.

The Executive Director will lead Alta Community/LocoL through its next stage of organizational development, strengthening the systems, partnerships, revenue, team, and strategy required to deliver sustainable community impact. The Executive Director will have overall responsibility for organizational leadership, fundraising and earned-revenue growth, financial stewardship, program quality and impact, team development, and external relationships.

This is an opportunity for a hands-on, entrepreneurial leader who can move comfortably between long-term strategy and practical execution. The successful candidate will understand how to build an emerging nonprofit organization while respecting LocoL’s history, community relationships, culinary identity, and commitment to economic opportunity and food justice.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership, Strategy & Administration
In partnership with the board of directors, develop and execute a strategic plan for the next five years of growth and impact.
Ensure operational and programmatic alignment with the organization’s values and goals.
Engage the Board through quarterly meetings to facilitate effective org governance.
Improve and implement HR practices for employee success, including performance management, compensation and staffing, and employee development and retention.
Build and develop a high-performing, inclusive team, ensuring role clarity and fostering a culture of growth, accountability, and teamwork.
Ensure compliance with California employment requirements.

Fundraising, Communications & Financial Management
Develop and implement a revenue strategy including earned income meal contracts, grants, and individual giving to raise and sustainably expand ~$700K operating budget.
Build and maintain relationships with donors, foundations, and funding partners.
Strengthen partnerships with nonprofits, community leaders and hiring partners.
Leverage data to enhance organizational storytelling and external communications to grow awareness, convey impact to key stakeholders, and drive fundraising targets.
Oversee financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for fiscal sustainability, including cash-flow management, financial controls, monthly financial reporting and forecasting, grant reporting, insurance and risk management and earned income margins.
Ensure compliance with all appropriate tax and accounting standards, as well as nonprofit regulations, reporting, and best practices.
Oversee planning of fundraising and community events, as needed.

Program Development
Recruit and manage a new Program Manager to ensure organizational alignment and effective program delivery. Program Manager responsibilities include:
Manage six program staff members and develop a hiring plan to fill additional capacity needs within the organization.
Expand and refine programs that provide culinary training, cooking education, and affordable catering for nonprofits.
Ensure operational success for LocoL, including kitchen operations, quality control, menu development, budgets, vendor relationships and customer service.
Collaborate with chef leaders at LocoL to develop and implement a job training program, focusing on culinary skills, hospitality, and professional development.
Mentor and coach team members, many of whom are entering the workforce for the first time, to help them achieve their full potential.
Oversee outcome measurement to demonstrate effectiveness.

Required capabilities
Passion for community and workforce development, food justice, and economic empowerment.
Proven executive or senior leadership in nonprofit management, social enterprises, or related fields.
Experience partnering with board of directors and leading teams.
Strong track record in fundraising, grants, and financial management.
Excellent strategic thinking, communication, storytelling, and advocacy skills.

Strongly preferred capabilities
Social-enterprise leadership.
Food, culinary, hospitality, catering, or production experience.
Los Angeles or Watts community relationships.
Early-stage organizational building.
Brand and communications experience.
Government contracting or institutional meal contracts.

Compensation & Benefits
Salary Range: $90,000-$110,000 (commensurate with experience).
Stipend for healthcare.
Paid-time off and paid sick time.

﻿
How to Apply
Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to info@altacommunityla.org
with the subject line “Executive Director Application – LocoL.”
Priority will be given to applications received by August 31, 2026.

jobs.description:
About IMPACCT Brooklyn

IMPACCT Brooklyn is a nonprofit community development organization dedicated to building and preserving thriving, equitable, and affordable neighborhoods across Brooklyn. Through affordable housing development, community organizing, economic development, and supportive services, we work alongside residents to strengthen communities and expand opportunities. We are a collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven team committed to advancing equity in the communities we serve.

About the Role

IMPACCT Brooklyn is seeking a seasoned and mission-driven Chief Program Officer (CPO) to join our Leadership Team. Reporting to the Executive Director, the CPO will provide strategic and operational leadership across IMPACCT Brooklyn’s programs and services while building a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing team culture. The Chief Program Officer directly supervises program directors and managers and is responsible for staff development, performance management, training, and hiring. Working closely with the Executive Director and senior leadership team, the CPO will ensure programs are effectively managed, responsive to community needs, and aligned with IMPACCT Brooklyn’s mission and long-term goals.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the strategy, planning, implementation, and evaluation of IMPACCT Brooklyn’s programs and services.
Develop and strengthen operational systems that improve program quality, coordination, and accountability.
Foster a supportive, collaborative, and results-oriented workplace culture.
Oversee the launch and implementation of new programs and initiatives.
Contribute to grant writing, reporting, and program evaluation.
Manage program budgets and support program leaders in developing and monitoring team budgets.
Supervise, coach, and develop program directors and managers, including performance management and hiring.
Partner with senior leadership on organizational priorities and special projects that expand capacity and impact.
Oversee community-building, organizing, and advocacy initiatives, including campaigns focused on housing and supportive services.
Lead long-term program planning and the development of program strategies, goals, and performance measures.
Analyze program performance and outcomes to strengthen effectiveness and respond to emerging community needs.
Alongside the Executive Director, represent IMPACCT Brooklyn with community members, partners, funders, and other external stakeholders.
Build external partnerships and identify resources and opportunities that strengthen services for IMPACCT Brooklyn’s communities.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in public administration, education, social work, or a related field; equivalent professional experience in community development or nonprofit leadership will be considered in lieu of an advanced degree.
A minimum of five years of leadership experience in a nonprofit, school, or philanthropic setting, overseeing multiple programs or contracts.
Demonstrated cultural competence as it relates to community-based work.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint), with the ability to learn program databases and tracking systems.

Compensation & Benefits

The annual salary range for this position is $155,000 – $175,000. This range represents IMPACCT Brooklyn’s good-faith estimate of the salary for this role at the time of posting. Actual compensation within the range will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skills, as well as internal equity. IMPACCT Brooklyn also offers a comprehensive benefits package.

Work Environment

This position operates in an administrative office environment and routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, and filing cabinets. The noise level can range from moderate to loud due to open cubicle work areas, conversations, and general office activity. The role involves prolonged periods of sitting and working at a computer, with occasional standing, walking, bending, and reaching, and may occasionally require lifting and moving up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position. Travel to other IMPACCT Brooklyn facilities may be required.

Schedule

This is a full-time position. The standard days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with occasional evenings and weekends as needed. Travel may be expected.

How to Apply

To apply, complete an application and submit your resume and cover letter by visiting our career page at IMPACCT Brooklyn Careers. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. No phone calls, please.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer at The Opportunity Network
jobs.description:
The Opportunity Network ignites the drive, curiosity, and agency of underresourced students on their paths to and through college and into thriving careers, powered by our commitment to access and community.

About The Organization

Since its founding in 2003, The Opportunity Network (OppNet) has worked to close the opportunity gap by helping students from under-resourced communities and first-generation college students overcome barriers to higher education and professional match. OppNet reimagines networks as sources of power, combining intensive personal connections and professional relationships with hard skills and experience. Through its flagship NYC-based Fellows program—an intensive six-year experience beginning the summer after 10th grade—and its national capacity-building partnerships, OppNet has reached over 150,000 young people. The organization's results are clear: 98% of OppNet Fellows graduate from college within six years, and 91% secure interest-aligned employment or graduate school admission within six months of graduation, far outpacing national trends.

OppNet is embarking on a pivotal chapter focused on deepening its national impact and expanding college and career success. To guide this future growth, OppNet is currently executing a clear three-pillared operational playbook: strengthening long-term financial sustainability, maximizing post-secondary and program outcomes, and building the internal systems and infrastructure required to optimize the organization for scale.

By reinforcing these operational and programmatic baselines, OppNet is actively evolving its proprietary Career Fluency® capacity-building model and developing regional hubs to ensure consistent, high-quality delivery across multiple markets. This structural evolution positions OppNet to expand its strategic partnerships with high schools and anchor institutions, adapt its offerings to meet rapid, ahead-of-market workforce shifts, and step forward as a prominent external voice and thought leader in the career and economic mobility space.

To learn more about the organization and its impact, please visit opportunitynetwork.org.

About The Role

OppNet is seeking a balanced, strategic, and forward-thinking Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to guide the organization through an exciting period of external change and market evolution. Stepping into a highly collaborative ecosystem, the incoming CEO will partner with a deeply dedicated staff and an engaged Board of Directors to champion our mission and scale our impact. Skillfully balancing a dedication to OppNet's core regional programming and community-based anchor partnerships with national growth, the CEO will set and steward the vision for navigating the evolving economic and funding landscapes with agility, crystalizing our organizational identity in a dynamic market, and unlocking the full potential of an influential network of champions and philanthropic supporters.

This role presents a powerful dual mandate: serving as the chief external ambassador responsible for cultivating executive-level relationships, advancing strategic growth priorities, expanding and enhancing the OppNet brand, and diversifying revenue, while institutionalizing robust internal operational systems.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a proven leader to guide a highly respected organization through an exciting inflection point, strategically guiding the evolution of OppNet's programmatic and operational strategy in service of fieldwide impact. The incoming leader inherits a strong foundation: a deeply committed and active Board, a tenured and high-performing leadership team, a track record of proven outcomes, and a robust platform poised for national growth. This role is an invitation to shape the future of both the organization and the wider field. This is a rare opportunity to leverage a proven model, amplify a brand on a national stage, and further advance the field.

Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

External Leadership and Fundraising

Serve as OppNet's primary external voice, chief spokesperson, and principal fundraiser, collaborating with teams to champion the mission to media, constituents, and the public
In partnership with the board, design and execute a sophisticated fundraising strategy to cultivate and diversify new donor revenue streams across individuals, foundations, and corporate funders, with a personal focus on securing seven-figure gifts
Engage directly as the lead ambassador in high-value donor relationships, modeling innovative philanthropic practices aligned with core organizational values
Oversee the overarching brand, marketing, and external communications strategy to secure OppNet's reputation as a prominent national thought leader in college and career Success

Organizational Strategy, Board Engagement & Team Leadership

Maintain a transparent relationship with the Board of Directors, designing engagement strategies that actively activate and leverage their unique talents, networks, and fundraising capabilities.
Collaborate with senior leadership to execute and evolve the strategic plan, entering shared decision-making while ensuring that the students and communities served remain the focal point of the work
Ensure the organization remains responsive to shifts in the postsecondary and workforce landscape, supporting executive leaders in developing and implementing strategies that address emerging trends such as generative AI
Lead, coach, and empower a long-tenured executive team, fostering an internal culture of continuous development, collaboration, and high morale across all levels.
Nurture a data-driven culture that leverages institutional learning to maintain exceptional student outcomes while navigating economic and educational landscape shifts.
In partnership with senior leadership, strengthen internal systems, scale operational infrastructure, and manage organizational risk and facilities to sustainably support a growing national footprint.

Who You'll Work With

You will report to a deeply invested and engaged Board of Directors
.

You will supervise an incredible team of tenured professionals, including the Chief Innovation Officer, Chief Program Officer, Chief Development Officer, and the Chief Operations Officer.

Required Skills And Experience

A minimum of 15 years of professional experience, including at least 7+ years in senior-most leadership roles (CEO, Executive Director, C-suite, or equivalent) navigating organizational growth, complexity, or transformation
A definitive track record of fundraising excellence with proven success personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing major gifts, specifically including seven-figure institutional, corporate, or individual funding streams.
Proven track record of designing, implementing, and executing multi-year strategic plans, with a demonstrated ability to future-proof an organization and align diverse stakeholders through influence and collaboration
Exceptional capacity to lead comprehensive change management, optimizing internal infrastructure, establishing formal systems, and successfully steering an organization through shifting external landscapes
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the executive presence and sophistication required to serve as a high-profile national advocate, thought leader, and media spokesperson
Extensive experience managing, coaching, and empowering high-performing senior executives; a proven ability to balance a culture of shared decision-making with robust performance accountability and professional bench-strength development.
Demonstrated experience leading organizational strategy through an active racial equity lens, with the cultural fluency required to authentically connect with, advocate for, and center communities of color and historically underrepresented youth.

This role is based in New York, New York and the organization currently operates in a remote-hybrid model with an expectation to be at external meetings regularly and in the office on an as-needed basis.

BACKGROUND

The Organization

Camp Judaea (“CJ”) is a vibrant nonprofit Jewish overnight summer camp located on 158 acres in the beautiful Blue Ridge Mountains near Hendersonville, North Carolina. Camp Judaea is a leading Jewish camp in the Southeast, where Jewish identity and community are at the heart of everything we do. Camp Judaea’s Mission

Camp Judaea’s mission is to provide a safe, fun, nurturing community where children, teens, and young adults grow as individuals, build lifelong friendships, develop leadership skills, and establish enduring connections with Judaism, Israel, and the natural environment.

Camp Judaea’s core values — community, leadership, joyful Judaism, and a love and connection with Israel — have guided camp life since the organization’s founding. Camp Judaea operates under the governance of a volunteer Board of Directors and is currently in an exciting period of strength.

Recent milestones include: twelve new cabins constructed, completed and paid for within the last three years; a recently completed Facilities Master Plan; a newly established development infrastructure; and a comprehensive multi-year strategic plan adopted by the Board. Camp Judaea is seeking a leader who is poised to take the organization’s vision to the next level. Building on disciplined fundraising experience, this role demonstrates consistent execution of donor strategy, consistent use of CRM systems, and sound fundraising judgment, with an increased expectation and demonstrated readiness to solicit larger, more complex gifts. The Executive Director, U.S. Policy & Government Affairs, serves as AMR Action Fund’s External Affairs team member responsible for developing and executing our policy, government affairs, and advocacy strategy in the United States. Primary Responsibilities

Policy Leadership

Develop and lead the AMR Action Fund's long-term US policy strategy in alignment with the Fund’s mission.
Advise the Fund’s executive leadership and the Board of Directors on US policy trends, legislative developments, geopolitical issues, and emerging opportunities affecting antimicrobial innovation.

Government Affairs & Legislative Strategy

Develop and execute comprehensive US federal advocacy and lobbying strategies supporting legislative pull incentives, including initiatives such as the PASTEUR Act and related reimbursement reforms.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with members of Congress, Congressional committees, Executive Branch agencies, and senior federal policymakers.
Lead high-level engagement with federal agencies including HHS, CMS, CDC, NIH, BARDA, FDA, ASPR, OMB, and other relevant government entities.
Develop U.S. policy positions and advocacy strategies related to antimicrobial reimbursement, procurement, regulatory modernization, preparedness, biodefense, and healthcare financing.
Represent AMR Action Fund in Congressional briefings, hearings, policy roundtables, and strategic stakeholder meetings.

External Affairs & Coalition Leadership

Lead the Fund's participation in major U.S. industry coalitions and policy alliances.
Develop strategic alliances with U.S. trade associations and trusted third parties in the AMR space.
Build consensus among diverse stakeholders to advance shared policy priorities.
Represent the Fund on advisory committees, steering committees, and external boards at the direction of the CEO and COO.

Policy Research & Evidence Generation

Contribute to the Fund's policy research agenda to support evidence-based advocacy in the United States.
Support the Fund’s policy positions with rigorous scientific, economic, and health policy evidence.

Strategic Communications

Coordinate with Executive Director, Communications and Media Relations to develop integrated policy communications strategies and materials, including briefings, white papers, position papers, policy briefs, and similar materials; and to build the Fund's reputation as a trusted thought leader in antimicrobial innovation policy.

Organizational Leadership

Contribute to a high-performing policy and External Affairs function.
Engage and manage external consultants, lobbying firms, research organizations, and policy contractors.
Contribute to departmental strategy, operating plans, performance metrics, and budgets.

Qualifications

Eight to twelve years of progressively responsible leadership experience in health policy, government affairs, biotechnology, pharmaceutical policy, or related fields.

Deep understanding of U.S. healthcare policy, pharmaceutical reimbursement, and federal legislative processes.
Experience engaging senior government officials, policymakers, and executive leadership.

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with experience presenting to executive audiences.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex scientific, economic, and policy information into actionable recommendations.

Advanced degree in public policy, public health, economics, biomedical sciences, political science, or related field.

Knowledge of global health security and pandemic preparedness.
Experience with venture capital or biotechnology investment ecosystems.
Established network within Congress, HHS, CMS, FDA, BARDA, NIH, and related agencies.
Record of peer-reviewed publications, policy reports, or nationally recognized thought leadership.

About The Organization

Since its founding in 2003, The Opportunity Network (OppNet) has worked to close the opportunity gap by helping students from under-resourced communities and first-generation college students overcome barriers to higher education and professional match. OppNet reimagines networks as sources of power, combining intensive personal connections and professional relationships with hard skills and experience. Through its flagship NYC-based Fellows program—an intensive six-year experience beginning the summer after 10th grade—and its national capacity-building partnerships, OppNet has reached over 150,000 young people. The organization's results are clear: 98% of OppNet Fellows graduate from college within six years, and 91% secure interest-aligned employment or graduate school admission within six months of graduation, far outpacing national trends.

OppNet is embarking on a pivotal chapter focused on deepening its national impact and expanding college and career success. To guide this future growth, OppNet is currently executing a clear three-pillared operational playbook: strengthening long-term financial sustainability, maximizing post-secondary and program outcomes, and building the internal systems and infrastructure required to optimize the organization for scale.

By reinforcing these operational and programmatic baselines, OppNet is actively evolving its proprietary Career Fluency® capacity-building model and developing regional hubs to ensure consistent, high-quality delivery across multiple markets. This structural evolution positions OppNet to expand its strategic partnerships with high schools and anchor institutions, adapt its offerings to meet rapid, ahead-of-market workforce shifts, and step forward as a prominent external voice and thought leader in the career and economic mobility space.

To learn more about the organization and its impact, please visit opportunitynetwork.org.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a proven leader to guide a highly respected organization through an exciting inflection point, strategically guiding the evolution of OppNet's programmatic and operational strategy in service of fieldwide impact. The incoming leader inherits a strong foundation: a deeply committed and active Board, a tenured and high-performing leadership team, a track record of proven outcomes, and a robust platform poised for national growth. This role is an invitation to shape the future of both the organization and the wider field. This is a rare opportunity to leverage a proven model, amplify a brand on a national stage, and further advance the field.

External Leadership and Fundraising

.

Policy Leadership

Experience engaging senior government officials, policymakers, and executive leadership.

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with experience presenting to executive audiences.

Advanced degree in public policy, public health, economics, biomedical sciences, political science, or related field.

Record of peer-reviewed publications, policy reports, or nationally recognized thought leadership.

Arvum Senior Living proudly manages Assisted Living and Memory Care communities across 8 different states, representing over 2,000 units throughout the Gulf Coast and Midwest region. As part of one of the largest senior living organizations in the country, Arvum communities have earned Great Place to Work® certifications from 2022–2026. At Arvum, your purpose and your growth are important to us. We continually aspire and invest in learning and development opportunities that support our team members’ professional growth, ensuring every Team Member can build a rewarding and enriching career.

Discover Your Purpose with Us at

The Welstone at Mission Crossing!

As Executive Director
, you’ll play an essential role in enriching the lives of seniors, creating meaningful connections, and making a difference every single day.

Your Role

As the Executive Director,
your role includes providing strategic and operational leadership to ensure exceptional service, financial performance, and a vibrant community culture. You will represent the community externally, foster collaboration internally, and lead by example through clear communication, accountability, and compassionate leadership.

Position Highlights

Status: Full-Time, Exempt
Schedule: Traditional leadership workweek with flexibility required based on business and operational needs, including Manager on Duty hours and on-call availability for emergency situations
Location: Mission, KS
Rate of Pay: $90,000 base salary + 20% Executive Director annual bonus potential
Travel: On-site/community-based; less than 10% travel

Why You'll Love This Community

Welcome to The Welstone at Mission Crossing, where freedom, comfort, and connection come together for an inspiring independent lifestyle. Located just minutes from Overland Park and Kansas City, our Independent Living community offers spacious apartment homes, resort-style amenities, and a warm, engaging environment designed for active adults. Here, residents enjoy chef-prepared dining, a dynamic calendar of social events, and maintenance-free living that lets you focus on what matters most: enjoying life your way.

As one of the best options for Independent Senior Living in Overland Park, KS, The Welstone combines exceptional value with Discovery’s signature lifestyle programs, including Sensations Dining, Dimensions Health & Wellness, and Celebrations Activities & Events. Every detail is designed to make each day vibrant, fulfilling, and worry-free.

What You’ll Do

Operational Leadership

Oversee day-to-day operations across all departments to ensure efficiency, compliance, and alignment with budgeted goals
Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations, as well as organizational and ownership standards
Maintain full responsibility for community financials, budgets, and operational performance metrics
Drive achievement of NOI, occupancy, and resident engagement targets
Monitor and manage operating costs, labor, and collections in alignment with financial expectations

Customer-Focused Culture

Champion a resident-centered model of care that prioritizes service, dignity, and engagement
Foster a supportive environment for residents, families, and team members alike
Support all program areas—clinical, memory care, dining, and life enrichment—with functional oversight
Hold regular Town Hall and/or Resident Council meetings, and ensure family communications and care plan reviews are consistent

Team & Talent Development

Provide visible leadership to department heads and community team members
Hire, train, develop, and coach staff to achieve high performance and job satisfaction
Implement policies and procedures that promote compliance, accountability, and professional growth
Support an inclusive, collaborative, and performance-driven work culture

Business Development & Sales Strategy

Partner with the sales team to drive occupancy and maximize top-line revenue
Contribute to pricing strategy and evaluate local market trends to maintain competitive positioning
Cultivate and maintain relationships within the community to support lead generation and referrals
Lead external business development strategy with clear accountabilities and measurable outcomes

Assisted Living / Memory Care (as applicable)

Ensure compliance with state AL/MC regulations, policies, and resident documentation
Lead monthly “at-risk” meetings and family engagement efforts
Oversee specialized programming (e.g., SHINE® Memory Care) to ensure effectiveness
Ensure wellness and care plans are properly implemented and tracked

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Hospitality, or related field preferred
Minimum 3 years of management experience, with at least 2 years as an Executive Director in senior living
Proven success in census growth, operational leadership, and financial management
Strong team leadership skills with experience in hiring, performance management, and coaching
Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
Experience with Medicaid (a plus, depending on state)
Participation in rotating on-call schedule and Manager on Duty (MOD) coverage required

Why Join Us

Discovery Senior Living Earned Coveted Great Place to Work Certification for 2025-2027!

A large part of what makes Discovery different from other companies in this industry is our willingness to embrace change. At Discovery Senior Living, we are constantly challenging how we are doing things to ensure the lifestyle we are offering our residents is absolutely the greatest value proposition in the marketplace. It’s just as important to us that the environment and culture for our team members are constantly refreshed. In addition, embracing and even encouraging change brings a never-ending supply of new energy to our business and our culture. That energy translates to other far-reaching positive impacts on our residents as well as our team members.

Find out what makes working at Discovery unique in the world of senior living. Discover Your Purpose!

Our Culture & Values

So often, what brings people together is deeply rooted in who we are and what we stand for. And at Discovery Senior Living, we’re unified by certain, core values, which we call our “Pillars of Excellence.” They make up the fabric of our company, and include TEAMWORK, INTEGRITY, PERFORMANCE, ACCOUNTABILITY, COMPASSION, HARD WORK and CREATIVITY.

Individually, they are our virtues, and together, they make up a roadmap which helps us foster innovation and success.

For eligible employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes competitive pay, medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) with employer match, paid training and career growth opportunities, wellness-related benefits, and additional support through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
